title: Review of c37's lone-cell negative: replicated at mu=2 on fresh seed 7. The three transplanted lone cells grow 11-62x and are torn up within 40-45 t after 0.49-0.76 diameters, while the same cells left in their crowd move 0.24-2.4; no lone cell swims
summary: Grew the claimed world (20261026T0227-c29-kernel-ring-screen/world.py with drive kernel, mu 1, kd 0.08, chi 5) from noise on seed 7 to t=2400 (labkit pack_seed7: 129 cells, 242 splits, 9 persistent, 27 tracks moved >= 1 body length) and ran the author's isolate_p.py with ISO_P mu=2, vmax=1 (sample every 5 t), 3 median cells (area 62 px), followed 400 t. Isolated: cells 14, 39 and 49 grow to 10.8x, 32x and 62x their area and are lost within 40-45 t (the tracked body breaks up), with net travel 0.65, 0.49 and 0.76 diameters. In place, at the same mu: 2.37 diameters before a split at t+250, 0.24 before a split at t+75, and 1.49 net (4.0 path) surviving 400 t. Same pattern as the finding: in fresh substrate a lone cell's growth outruns its motion, and the stronger drive does not make it swim.

observations.M: rerun/lone_mu2_s7.json: isolated net 0.49-0.76 diameters (cells lost at t+40-45, area x11-62) vs in place 0.24-2.37

seeds_run.result: pass: no lone cell swims at mu=2

controls_run.M: in-place arm of isolate_p.py (same cells, same mu, left in their crowd)

not_checked: lower DS or a depleted bath
verdicts.limitation: One seed and mu=2 only. On this seed the isolated cells are lost faster (40-45 t) than on the author's seed 5 (up to 335 t), so they had less time to travel. 'Lost' means the tracker lost the body, which the author's images show to be tearing of the grown front; I did not draw the strip.
